newsitem.title: USA: Anti-gaming bill advances in Louisiana Senate.
newsitem.headline: Anti-gaming bill advances in Louisiana Senate.

text.p: Louisiana's Senate Judiciary Committee has approved a bill that would outlaw casino gambling, video poker and riverboat casinos.
The bill passed the committee in a 4-2 vote Tuesday despite objections from opponents who said it would cost the state $500 million in gaming revenue.
The bill now heads to the full Senate.
The bill (SB1200) by Sen. Tommy Casanova, R-Crowley, would shut down the New Orleans land casino immediately, end video poker in two years and eliminate riverboat casinos in five years.
Committee Chairman Sen. Don Cravins, D-Lafayette, predicted the bill would fail, but added that it would force lawmakers to consider the social impact of gambling.
